Top Behavioral Questions Have a real story ready for each of these ten. Tell me about yourself. Walk me through your background, key experiences, and what brings you here today. The STAR Method Structure your answers for clarity and impact. Situation Set the context. Where and when did it happen? Task What was your responsibility or goal? Action What steps did you take? Be specific. Result What was the outcome? Share impact, metrics, or key learnings. TIPS TO ACE BEHAVIORAL INTERVIEWS Understand the question. Clarify if needed. Use the STAR method for structured answers. Be specific and honest. Share real examples. Focus on your actions, not the team's. Quantify results when possible. Show your thought process and learnings. Keep it concise: 1.5–2 minutes is ideal. Practice out loud. Preparation builds confidence. More Questions by Theme High-impact behavioral questions, grouped. Ownership & Accountability Tell me about a time you took ownership of a project. Tell me about a time you went above and beyond. Tell me about a time you held yourself accountable. Problem Solving & Thinking Tell me about a time you analyzed data to make a decision. Tell me about a time you had to make a tough decision. Tell me about a time you identified a problem before others did. Collaboration & Influence Tell me about a time you influenced someone's opinion. Tell me about a time you worked with a difficult teammate. Tell me about a time you had to gain buy-in for an idea. Adaptability & Learning Tell me about a time things didn't go as planned. Tell me about a time you adapted to change. Tell me about a time you received feedback. Customer Focus & Impact Tell me about a time you delivered excellent customer service. Tell me about a time you solved a customer's problem. Tell me about a time you created value for users/customers. Extra tips & reminders Review your past projects and experiences. Prepare stories in advance for each theme. Tailor examples to the role and company. Stay positive. No blaming or badmouthing. End with key learnings or impact. Remember: “Anyone can say they are a good problem solver or a great leader. Your stories prove it.”

PART 2 · LEADERSHIP PRINCIPLES Amazon Leadership Principles The foundation of how Amazon thinks, decides, and acts. Principles 1–8. Customer Obsession Leaders start with the customer and work backwards. They earn trust, listen deeply, and deliver what customers need, often before they ask. Understand customers deeply. Earn trust through actions. Innovate to delight customers. Ownership Leaders are owners. They think long term and don't say “that's not my job.” They act on behalf of the entire company. Take ownership beyond your role. Solve problems without waiting. Think long term. Invent and Simplify Leaders expect and create innovation. They look for simpler solutions and remove complexity. Challenge the status quo. Encourage new ideas. Simplify and focus on what matters. Are Right, A Lot Leaders have strong judgment and make highquality decisions with available information. Make decisions with conviction. Disagree and commit. Learn and adjust quickly. Learn and Be Curious Leaders never stop learning. They are curious about new possibilities and seek to improve themselves. Ask questions. Seek different perspectives. Learn continuously. Hire and Develop the Best Leaders raise the bar with every hire and invest in developing people to reach their full potential. Hire the best. Give honest feedback. Develop future leaders. Insist on the Highest Standards Leaders set high standards and continuously raise the bar. They focus on quality, always. Deliver high-quality results. Pay attention to detail. Continuously improve. Think Big Leaders think beyond today and beyond their team. They look for big, bold opportunities. Think long term. Take smart risks. Imagine what's possible. PART 2 · LEADERSHIP PRINCIPLES Amazon Leadership Principles Principles 9–16. Bias for Action Speed matters. Leaders move fast, make decisions, and adjust along the way. Act quickly. Don't wait for perfection. Learn from doing. Frugality Leaders do more with less. They are good stewards of resources and respect the company's money and tools. Avoid waste. Be resourceful. Focus on impact, not expense. Earn Trust Leaders are honest, transparent, and respectful. They listen, admit mistakes, and build strong relationships. Communicate openly. Show respect. Build trust with actions. Dive Deep Leaders operate at all levels and stay connected to details, metrics, and ground reality. Dig into data. Understand root causes. Don't rely on assumptions. Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit Leaders respectfully challenge decisions when needed, then fully commit to the decision, even if they disagreed. Challenge decisions respectfully. Commit once decided. Put the team and mission first. Deliver Results Leaders focus on outcomes and impact. They hold themselves and others accountable. Set clear goals. Hold to commitments. Deliver for customers. Strive to be Earth's Best Employer Leaders create a safe, inclusive, and highperforming workplace where people can do their best work. Value and respect people. Promote inclusion and diversity. Create a great place to work. Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility As we grow, our impact grows. Leaders act on behalf of society and future generations. Think about the long-term impact. Be a good steward. Make sustainable choices. Use these principles every day. They guide our decisions, actions, and culture.

10 Powerful Questions Smart questions show ownership, curiosity, business understanding and long-term thinking. For all roles. If I join this role, what would success look like in the first 90 days? Shows you are thinking about delivering value and taking ownership. Demonstrates problem-solving mindset and helps you understand real work. Makes the interviewer imagine you in the role and creates a consultative discussion. Shows engineering maturity and starts a meaningful technical discussion. Great for senior backend / technical roles. Reveals system design complexity. Shows understanding of real-world engineering tradeoffs. Shows strategic thinking and long-term interest. Signals leadership potential and interest in decision making. Senior & Staff Candidates Additional questions for senior and staff-level roles. What are the highest-impact initiatives planned for the team this year? Shows you think about impact and priorities. Shows interest in growth and leadership path. Shows interest in cross-team collaboration and the bigger picture. THE POWERFUL CLOSING QUESTION “Based on our discussion today, do you have any concerns about my experience or fit for the role that I can address right now?” Shows confidence. Gives you a chance to handle objections. Many candidates never ask this. Best 5 for Software Engineers If you only have time for five, ask these. 1 What would success look like in the first 90 days? 2 What are the biggest challenges the team is solving right now? 3 What differentiates top performers on this team? 4 How does the team balance feature delivery with technical debt? 5 Based on our discussion, do you have any concerns about my fit that I can address? QUESTIONS TO AVOID How soon do people get promoted? How many leaves do I get? (Unless discussing offer details) Do I have to work hard? What time can I leave? Questions already answered during the interview. Asking thoughtful questions shows that you are not just looking for a job, you are looking to make an impact and grow with the organization.
